for DAMAGING WINDS and LARGE HAILSTONES
The State Emergency Service advises that people should:
* Secure or put away loose items around your property.
* Move cars under cover or away from trees.
* Keep clear of fallen power lines.
* Stay indoors, away from windows, while storms are nearby.

warning-info.text: The next warning is due to be issued by 8:25 pm.

text.p: Check https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts. Warnings are also available through TV and Radio broadcasts or call 1300 659 210. The Bureau and State Emergency Service would appreciate warnings being broadcast regularly.

forecast-period.text: Severe thunderstorms are approaching Adelaide and Mount Barker.

text.p: A more general severe thunderstorm warning is also current for the Adelaide Metropolitan, Mount Lofty Ranges, Yorke Peninsula, Mid North and parts of the Eastern Eyre Peninsula, Flinders, Murraylands, Upper South East and North West Pastoral districts.

The Bureau of Meteorology warns that, at 7:25 pm, severe thunderstorms likely to produce damaging winds and large hailstones were detected near Longwood and the middle of the Gulf. These thunderstorms are moving towards the east to southeast. They are forecast to affect Adelaide City, Glenelg, Mount Barker and Salisbury by 7:55 pm and Woodside, Gumeracha and Lobethal by 8:25 pm.
